描述_EN: by the tang dynasty (618-906 ad), from which this textile dates, there were a thousand caves decorated with religious scenes. most of the textiles from this site would have been used as banners or wrappers for religious texts. the site is also part of an area of central asia we now call the silk road. the insides of each cave-shrine were painted with coloured murals, some of which survive to this day. camels and horses were used as pack animals and merchants passed the goods from oasis to oasis. this textile was brought back from central asia by the explorer and archaeologist sir marc aurel stein (1862-1943). the most notable item traded was silk. the silk road was also important for the exchange of ideas. the cave of the thousand buddhas, of which there are several in the area, are named after a legend concerning a monk’s dream of a thousand buddhas appearing on a cloud to one side of the valley where the caves are situated. while silk textiles travelled west from china, buddhism entered china from india in this way. it was recovered from cave 17 of the mogao grottoes, near the oasis town of dunhuang. this term was first used by the german scholar ferdinand von ricthofen (1833-1905) and it refers to a series of overland trade routes that crossed asia from china to europe. this location is a shrine site and one of china’s great buddhist pilgrimage structures.the shrines were carved out of the gravel conglomerate naturally occurring in the region.
描述_ZN: 到了唐代（公元618-906年），也就是这幅纺织品的年代，有一千个洞穴被装饰有宗教场景。 该遗址的大部分纺织品都是作为宗教文本的旗帜或包装物。 该遗址也是我们现在称之为丝绸之路的中亚地区的一部分。 每个洞窟神龛的内部都绘有彩色壁画，其中有些壁画至今仍在。 年，骆驼和马被用作驮运动物，商人们在绿洲之间传递货物。 年，这个纺织品被探险家和考古学家Marc Aurel Stein先生（1862-1943）从中亚带回来。 年，最引人注目的贸易项目是丝绸。 年：丝绸之路对于思想的交流也很重要。 千佛洞，在该地区有几个，是根据一个传说命名的，说的是一个和尚梦见千佛出现在山谷一侧的云彩上，洞中有千佛。 丝织品从中国西行，佛教通过这种方式从印度进入中国。 它是在敦煌绿洲镇附近的莫高窟第17窟发现的。 这个词最早是由德国学者Ferdinand von Ricthofen（1833-1905）使用的，它指的是一系列从中国到欧洲穿越亚洲的陆上贸易路线。 这个地方是一个圣地，也是中国伟大的佛教朝圣建筑之一。圣地是由该地区自然形成的砂砾岩雕刻而成的。
